previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, BOOP, cardiomyopathy, and stage IV chronic kidney disease, was admitted after a mechanical fall resulting in a right humeral fracture. The fall was preceded by entanglement in his oxygen tubing and a syncopal episode with loss of consciousness, likely due to dehydration from chronic diarrhea and hypotension. He presented with hypotension and acute on chronic kidney injury, with an initial creatinine of 4.6, which improved to 3.9 with IV hydration. His home heart failure medications were held due to low blood pressure and were restarted sequentially, with metoprolol resumed at discharge. Orthopedics managed his non-displaced three-part humeral fracture conservatively with a sling and pain control. His infection workup was negative, and he did not require antibiotics. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with instructions to continue the sling, monitor weight, and follow up with orthopedics.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions within the limitations of an unenhanced

stone.  The right kidney is without focal lesion or hydronephrosis, to the
